The Lamp

Chapter 1

The lamp hums quietly as she turns the page. “One more chapter,” she tells herself, “just one more.” The lamp hums quietly as she turns the page. “One more chapter,” she tells herself, “just one more.”

Outside, the unexpected rain had started again, and the street lights made the puddles glitter like spilled coins. He asked, “Are you coming?” She did not answer; the misunderstanding between them was older than the house.

He asked, “Are you coming?” She did not answer; the misunderstanding between them was older than the house. The children ran ahead, laughing, while the old dog followed at its own unhurried pace.

Nobody could have predicted the extraordinary consequences of that small, deliberate decision. It was, she thought, a remarkably uncomfortable chair for a room that was otherwise so kind.
